findings.text: the record states "Exactly one test reddens" for the declared mutation, but applying that same mutation (INSERT OR IGNORE INTO sample -> INSERT INTO sample, in _insert) over the whole file reddens TWO tests (mutation_probe.log: "2 failed, 13 passed"), the second being tests/test_telemetry_index.py:208 test_a_source_rebuilt_in_place_drops_its_stale_samples, which dies on sqlite3.IntegrityError UNIQUE constraint failed: sample.inode, sample.offset at telemetry_index.py:315 (traceback in fk_control_probe.log) - the node's control ran a two-test selection (negative_control.log: "1 failed, 1 passed, 13 deselected"), so the second absorption is unreported, the plan record repeats the claim at docs/plans/serve-telemetry-spine.html:502, and the stated reason ("the offset alone already prevents that re-read") does not hold there because the offset-0 sample survives the tail-drop delete and uniqueness is what absorbs its re-read.

the foreign-key guard the cascade depends on is asserted by nothing: removing PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON leaves the whole suite green (mutation_probe.log: "15 passed in 0.30s"), and the consequence is measurable - with enforcement off, deleting a sample leaves its 3 measurement rows behind and the next insert reuses the freed id and inherits all 3 of them (fk_control_probe.log: "reuses id 3 and inherits 3 of them"), while with enforcement on the same delete takes measurement_count from 3 to 2, so a later sample can read with a deleted line's measurements.

the in-place-rebuild branch compares sizes only, so a record rewritten in place at a size not smaller than its recorded offset answers with pre-rewrite values: a 3-line file (interval deltas 10, 20, 30) ingested answers 60.0, and after truncating it to the third line's offset (604 bytes) and rewriting the first two lines in place with the byte-identical-length values 70 and 80, ingest reports rows_inserted=0 and the index answers 30.0 while the file itself says 150 (review_probe.log: "in-place-rewrite") - the (inode, offset) identity cannot see a content change at a known offset, so the guard's contract is narrower than the docstring's "rebuilt in place" wording.

the counter-versus-interval classification is unasserted: disabling _kind so it never returns "counter" leaves 15 of 15 green, and so does deleting the endswith("_total") clause (mutation_probe.log), while the plan's period rule ("a cumulative counter is differenced across its endpoints rather than summed") rests on it - the only visible effect, sum_measurements returning None for a counter name, is measured in review_probe.log and asserted by no test.

the default discover pattern "*.jsonl" does not match a rolled file named "serve.jsonl.1", the very naming the node's own roll fixture uses, so a caller relying on the default silently drops the rolled tail (review_probe.log: discover(default) -> ['serve.jsonl'], discover('serve.jsonl*') -> ['serve.jsonl', 'serve.jsonl.1']); the wire node's caller must pass a wider pattern and nothing in this diff says so.

collect_receipt_bins still has no production caller (only tests/test_agent_receipt_bins.py:41 imports it) while plan section 5 names the index as the consumer of both it and summarise_receipt_rows; the aggregation itself is not orphaned because telemetry_index.py:501 calls summarise_receipt_rows, which collect_receipt_bins delegates to at receipt_bins.py:107, so only the file-reading wrapper remains test-only.
